item.title: Trump to hold summit with Xi, Putin in Shenzhen on Thursday, NY Post reports
item.description:
Nov 13 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump will hold a trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the annual APEC conference in Shenzhen on Thursday, the New York Post reported on Friday.

The trilateral discussion is expected to focus largely on developing an ambitious nuclear arms control pact, but discussions could also touch on North Korea and the Iran war, the Post reported.

Trump has already publicly indicated that he planned to meet with the two leaders.

item.title: Turkey, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
item.description:
Turkey and Qatar announced on Friday that they signed a mutual defence agreement, which they said was aimed at adopting a "unified position" in the face of an external attack.

The announcement came after Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan met Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul.

Erdogan had said the agreement would further strengthen ties between the regional allies, according to his office.

Qatar's ruler travelled to Istanbul after attending the United Nations COP31 climate summit in southern Turkey.

item.title: Spanish prosecutor favours extraditing pro-Palestinian US Cox Enterprises heir
item.description:
MADRID, Nov 13 (Reuters) - A Spanish prosecutor on Friday expressed support for a US request to extradite pro-Palestinian donor and multimillionaire US media heir James Cox Chambers Jr, in a case Chambers' defence says is politically motivated.

Spain's High Court will rule on the case in coming weeks. Government spokesperson Elma Saiz has said the cabinet would then make the final determination.

item.title: UN rights chief demands Houthis return body of Yemeni staff member
item.description:
GENEVA, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The UN's human rights chief on Friday demanded the return of the body of a Yemeni staff member of his office who died of unknown causes weeks ago after being held in Houthi custody for more than two years.

Mohammad el Shami's family learned of his death on October 30, more than a month after it occurred, but they have received no explanation of the cause or circumstances. El Shami had been held by the Houthi group since June ​6, 2024.

item.title: Turkey, Qatar sign mutual defence agreement, pledge unified stance against attack
item.description:
ISTANBUL, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defence agreement on Friday aimed at strengthening collective defence and promoting regional security, and pledged a unified stance against any external armed attack targeting either country, according to a joint statement issued after talks between their leaders.

The two sides agreed to consult on threats to their security, as well as regional and global security issues and defence policies, and to expand cooperation through joint military exercises, defence-industry cooperation and personnel training exchanges.

item.title: Judges close part of ICC Afghanistan investigations that could look at US troops
item.description: THE HAGUE, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Judges at the International Criminal Court have issued a decision to formally close part of the prosecutor's investigations into Afghanistan that previously looked at alleged crimes by US troops and to focusonly on actions of the Taliban since 2021, court documents show.

item.title: UN chief urges drastic emissions cuts as COP31 wrestles with fossil fuels
item.description:
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 13 (Reuters) - UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Friday called for an "immediate and drastic reduction" in greenhouse gas emissions, as divisions over fossil fuels dominated the first week of COP31 climate talks in Turkey.

Big fossil fuel producers and consumers at the talks are resisting any deal that would specify firm new targets or a shift away from oil, gas and coal, observers said as the first week of talks drew to a close.

item.title: Palestinian teen reunites with family after month in Israeli jail
item.description:
Looking tiny in his adult-size grey prison jumpsuit, 15-year-old Palestinian Ezzedine al-Lahalia appeared stunned as his mother embraced him after a month in an Israeli jail. 

His first request was a child's wish for his favourite food: stuffed cabbage and shawarma.

The teenager, who had been charged with throwing stones, was reunited with his family Thursday night in an emotional scene witnessed by an AFP photographer.

item.title: Gore blasts 'insane' Saudi veto power at climate talks
item.description:
Former US vice president Al Gore said it was "literally insane" that oil-producing nations such as Saudi Arabia could block global action against climate change, calling for sweeping reforms to UN negotiations.

Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, Gore said UN climate talks needed to replace the consensus-based decision-making system with a supermajority model.
